title: ‘It’s impactful’: Seattle Sports fans see a bright future at stadium gatherings
description: Two major sports events took place in Seattle on Saturday. The Super Bowl-winning Seahawks held their Fan Fest, and the Mariners celebrated 50 years of Seattle baseball as the team hosted the Tampa Bay Rays.
fullText:
Two major sports events took place in Seattle on Saturday. The Super Bowl-winning Seahawks held their Fan Fest, and the Mariners celebrated 50 years of Seattle baseball as the team hosted the Tampa Bay Rays.

Tens of thousands of fans attended both of those events, which took place virtually at the same time, right next to each other.

The sidewalks filled with streams of Seahawks fans with their sights set on Lumen Field, while the baseball faithful headed to T-Mobile Park:

For some fans, the choice between two beloved sports teams wasn't so easy.

"Go 'Hawks, go Mariners baby!" said Preston Erikson, who acknowledged it was impossible for him, his brother and their cousins to attend both. "No, we're not. We wish."

Fans of both teams acknowledged it was a fun problem to have. Seattle boasts a number of top-tier professional men's and women's sports teams, and it won rave reviews for its enthusiasm while hosting six World Cup matches.

"We are a great sports town. I just think- look across the street, you've got Mariners fans, you've got Seahawks fans. It just brings the whole city out. Everyone comes together," said Tijera Loggins.

Trey Erikson told KIRO 7 that there's something special about a sports town and the fans who support their teams.

"We've been in Seattle our whole lives, and it's just something where cultures come together, people come together. It's something words can't even describe. It's emotional. It's important, it's impactful, and it's powerful," he said.

There is an economic impact as well. Local shops and restaurants say business increases every time there's an event at Lumen or T-Mobile.

The economic impact of the World Cup alone here was predicted to be $850 million.

title: ODI Tri-series is back! ECB Chief says triangular ODI series' being planned after Shubman Gill comments
description: ECB chief Richard Gould confirms England remains open to reviving the triangular series. Get the details.
fullText:
ODI Tri-series is back! ECB Chief says triangular ODI series' being planned after Shubman Gill comments originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

ECB chief Gould confirms England remains open to tri-series fixtures.

India captain Shubman Gill wants multi-team tournaments back.

Several tri-series already scheduled under ICC's 2023-2027 FTP cycle.

England and Wales Cricket Board chief executive Richard Gould has responded positively to Indian ODI captain Shubman Gill's appeal for the return of triangular cricket tournaments, confirming that several tri-series fixtures are already lined up over the coming 12 to 18 months.

Gill has thrown his support behind the ICC's decision to leave the 50-over format untouched, describing the ODI World Cup as cricket's most prestigious global event. Rather than trimming matches down to 40 overs, he believes reviving multi-team formats like tri-series and quadrangular tournaments would do far more to reignite excitement around ODI cricket.

"I grew up watching 50-over cricket a lot, and it remained an integral part of my childhood," Gill said ahead of the first ODI in Birmingham against England. "When I think of the World Cup, the first thought that comes to mind is the 50-over World Cup. For me, the 50-over World Cup is the most prestigious World Cup. I don't think it should be changed to 40 overs."

Gill also fondly recalled watching several triangular series growing up, particularly those involving India, Australia and Sri Lanka, and described them as genuinely entertaining to follow.

"One thing is that we used to play a lot of triangular series and it was really fun to watch. India, Australia and Sri Lanka used to play those tournaments," he said.

"If I ever get a chance to play in a triangular series, it will be fun because you are not playing one team continuously. If we want to make this format more interesting, instead of having bilateral series, we can have triangular or quadrangular series. That'll be interesting to play and to watch."

MORE: India's 2036 Olympic bid receives ECB support

According to Dainik Jagran, Gould acknowledged that there's still room within international cricket's calendar for tri-series to make a comeback.

He noted that England's own scheduling priorities currently lean toward formats that don't stretch the calendar excessively, though the ECB remains open to exploring tri-series as a viable option going forward.

MORE: Brett Lee ignores Sachin Tendulkar as ex-Australia star names his pick

Several tri-series tournaments have already found their way back into cricket's calendar under the ICC's Future Tours Programme covering 2023 to 2027.

Pakistan hosted a tri-series in February 2025 involving New Zealand and South Africa, serving as a warm-up event ahead of that year's ICC Champions Trophy.

Looking further ahead, a T20I tri-series is scheduled for August-September 2026 in Windhoek, Namibia, bringing together South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, the three co-hosts of the 2027 World Cup.

Pakistan is also set to host another tri-nation series in October 2026, featuring two visiting nations as part of the broader FTP schedule.

MORE: 'Sooryavanshi has skill but…': Dhawan gives his verdict on Vaibhav

Gill's argument taps into something cricket fans have quietly missed for years. i.e. the unpredictability and variety that triangular tournaments once brought to the format.

Bilateral series are easy enough to slot into a calendar, but they rarely bring the kind of shifting challenge that comes from facing several different opponents within one tournament window. Tri-series used to deliver exactly that as teams had to constantly adjust their tactics against contrasting styles of different teams, which kept things interesting for viewers.

Bringing the format back on a larger scale won't be simple, though. Cricket's calendar is already stretched thin, and squeezing in more multi-team tournaments will be difficult. The cricket administrators should find a way to balance them against existing bilateral series and league commitments without burning out players further.

Gould's measured stance, leaving the door open for tri-series without treating them as an urgent priority, seems like a reasonable way forward. Done right, rather than tacked on as an afterthought in the schedule, this format could bring back some of the spark ODI cricket has been missing, without piling even more strain onto an already packed calendar.

title: Ben Simmons makes eye-opening Instagram post amid NBA comeback attempt
description: Ben Simmons shared a reflective message that hints at exactly where his head is as his comeback attempt continues to take shape.
fullText:
Ben Simmons makes eye-opening Instagram post amid NBA comeback attempt appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Ben Simmons is sending another signal that his NBA career is far from over. The former No. 1 overall pick shared a reflective message on Instagram Saturday, posting a photo of himself looking physically imposing near a basketball hoop alongside a caption that read as both a farewell to his turbulent past and a declaration of intent for what comes next.

"I wouldn't change the story," Simmons wrote on Instagram. "The highs, the lows, the pain, the time, the lessons, I embrace all of it. Every chapter built something in me that I couldn't have built any other way. Grateful for where I've been. Proud of where I stand. Ready for wherever this goes."

The post landed just days after he shared a photo of LeBron James' signature sneakers on his Instagram Story, another quiet hint that a return to the league, and possibly a reunion with his original franchise, remains on his mind.

Simmons has not played since appearing in 18 games for the Los Angeles Clippers during the 2024-25 season, averaging just 2.9 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 3.1 assists in 16.4 minutes. He sat out the entire 2025-26 campaign after his previous contract expired, but has repeatedly made clear in recent interviews that retirement is not on his mind.

Simmons' career has followed a dramatic arc since Philadelphia made him the top pick in the 2016 draft. He won Rookie of the Year and earned three All-Star selections behind his rare combination of size, playmaking, and defensive versatility, drawing comparisons to some of the league's most unique talents.

A mix of injuries, a well-documented mental health battle, and a messy split with the 76ers organization eventually derailed that trajectory, leading to his 2022 trade to the Brooklyn Nets and a steady decline in role and production ever since.

Now 30, Simmons appears intent on writing a new chapter. Speculation about a reunion with Philadelphia has picked up since LeBron James signed with the 76ers this offseason, given the two share the same representation in Rich Paul and Klutch Sports.

Whether that speculation turns into anything concrete remains unclear, but for a player once at the center of one of the NBA's most talked-about breakups, his latest message suggests he is done running from his past and ready to write whatever comes next.

While the New York Yankees remain a very competitive team in the American League, they have been trying to stay afloat despite three injuries to their offensive core.

Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Cody Bellinger remain out due to injury. Despite their absence, the Yankees have found ways to win baseball games.

Throughout their last eight games, New York has gone 5-3. It isn't ideal, but the Yankees are staying afloat enough to allow their stars to get healthy. The hope is that they can return at some point down the final stretch of the regular season heading into the playoffs.

On Saturday, August 8, New York revealed a new update about Stanton. He hasn't played a game since April 24 when he went down with a calf injury.

Aaron Boone, the Yankees' manager, revealed some new details about Stanton. His latest update provides some optimism about a potential return sooner rather than later.

He stated that Stanton jogged in the outfield on Friday and "started the introduction to some bases." Boone also said that "I expect him back here at some point. He'll be in there when the time's right."

Stanton is still a very feared player at the plate when healthy. He may be 36 years old now, but he's still capable of taking baseballs out of the park.

Prior to the injury, Stanton played in just 24 games. He hit three home runs to go along with 14 RBI and a slash line of .256/.302/.422. Adding his production back into the lineup would be a big step towards legitimate World Series contention for New York.

Fans across the baseball world were quick to make their comments heard on social media.

"Unbelievable how this dude can barely move every season. Was on a massive hall of fame trajectory," one fan wrote.

Another chimed in, "Imagine being an MLB player and being introduced to touching a base again due to a strained calf."

"I can't wait for this dead weight to no longer be a Yankee. All time bad acquisition. The NTC should never happen again for any contract," a third fan commented.

Yet another fan said, "Honestly these updates are ridiculous and the whole Stanton situation is absurd."

"Have this man strap up for the Old Timers game at this point," another comment read.

Needless to say, fans are frustrated with how much time Stanton has missed. At 36, recovering from an injury gets a bit more difficult. Hopefully, more good news will be coming regarding the slugger in the near future.

title: Cavaliers, Hawks, Clippers, Bucks in bidding war for $11M NBA champion, 23-year-old young star
description: The Cavaliers, Clippers, Bucks, and Hawks are in need of a starting wing. It seems they are fighting it out for one of the top remaining free agents.
fullText:
Cavaliers, Hawks, Clippers, Bucks in bidding war for $11M NBA champion, 23-year-old young star originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

NBA rosters for the upcoming season are still being adjusted with free agency continuing to unfold. LeBron James' decision held up the process for several organizations and players looking for new homes, and there are still plenty of major moves left to be made.

One player searching for a potential new home is Peyton Watson, who is a restricted free agent. Watson and his camp are reportedly seeking a hefty contract as negotiations continue.

"Peyton Watson and his camp want something in that $28 million north range and the offers so far have been fluctuating between that $20-24 million per year range… When you're Peyton Watson, you want more than Christian Braun," ClutchPoints' Brett Siegel wrote.

The biggest challenge for Watson is that, as a restricted free agent, he cannot simply choose whichever team he wants. A deal has to be worked out between Watson and the Denver Nuggets, which would likely come in the form of a sign-and-trade. However, with Denver in a difficult financial situation, there has been discussion about Watson potentially accepting his qualifying offer instead.

"The top restricted free agents — Jalen Duren, Peyton Watson and Bennedict Mathurin — are now all considering taking their qualifying offers to become unrestricted in 2027. As negotiations stall out across the board, these three could become trendsetters against the RFA process," NBA reporter Evan Sidery posted.

Denver does not want to lose Watson, but the organization's financial situation could ultimately force its hand. Teams such as the Atlanta Hawks, Cleveland Cavaliers, Milwaukee Bucks and Los Angeles Clippers have all expressed interest in getting a deal done for the young wing.

"That is why teams like the LA Clippers, Milwaukee Bucks, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Atlanta Hawks have all expressed sign-and-trade interest in Watson over the last month. Interest from the Clippers, Bucks, and Cavs is real, yet there are still some limitations to each potential sign-and-trade scenario," Siegel wrote.

The teams clearly want Watson, but the Nuggets are not going to let him leave unless they receive a package they believe is worth it.

Watson has earned $11 million throughout his young NBA career. Given Denver's current financial situation, the Nuggets also do not have much flexibility to work with in a potential trade. For now, the Hawks, Cavaliers, Clippers and Bucks will continue battling for Watson's services. If none of those teams can get a sign-and-trade completed, Watson could ultimately take his qualifying offer and enter unrestricted free agency in 2027.

title: Matchday Musings: Fun In The Sun As The Lads See Off Lens!
description: A convincing win in France that’ll hopefully ease transfer worries and remind us to enjoy how great this side is!
fullText:
Yesterday's match was a rarity for me: a pre-season game that looked to have something approaching an actual atmosphere.

I wasn't overly fussed about the Lads' North American tour.

I'm pleased it all went well but sinking $25 Michelob Lights with a side of grits in the PricewaterhouseCoopers THUNDERDOME isn't my idea of fun. Knocking the froth off a few Saint-Omers in glorious sunshine, however? Yes, please. Incredibly jealous of all the lovely lads and lasses out there, and a comfortable 2-0 win was just the cherry on top for them all. Santé!

Even with all the usual caveats around pre-season friendlies — "Results don't matter", "It's about fitness", etc, etc — I feel yesterday's friendly was as close to being important as you can get this time of year.

Lens have been a consistently strong side for a number of years and are looking to retain their title of "Best Of The Rest After PSG" as well as having a Champions League campaign ahead of them.

They're no mugs, as the old adage goes, and a strong Sunderland side (more on this later), Granit Xhaka's first run-out and a packed Stade Bollaert-Delelis added on extra layers of intrigue to the fixture.

Maybe that sense of importance rubbed off on the players too as we were at it straight from kick-off.

Our pressing throughout the game in particular was a delight to watch. We largely controlled the first half without being dominant and, while it looked like we still had gears to move up through, Lens barely landed a punch.

Xhaka was Xhaka, Brian Brobbey was Brobbey and Trai Hume was Hume, including a gorgeous volley that left the crossbar quaking like Lewis Hall. Just lovely lads, aren't they? Thomas Meunier looked very accomplished, which you'd expect, and was unlucky to have his header chalked off.

After their subdued first half, Lens stepped it up after the break and it took us a little while to settle after Xhaka and Meunier went off, although we never looked anything other than comfortable at the back.

Robin Roefs didn't have a save to make until after the seventieth minute. We probably did lack something going forward so Régis Le Bris turned to Chris Rigg and Wilson Isidor, and it was this second round of subs that sealed the game.

Rigg continued his fine pre-season and just looks like the real deal the more you see of him. A lovely assist for Hume and a key role in creating the second for Isidor, and it just feels a huge season is ahead for Sunderland's favourite son.

Always lovely to see Isidor on the scoresheet and Le Bris was very firm afterwards in shutting down any talk of a move away which was nice to see. Isidor, to me, just feels like a Europa League striker and I can't wait to see whether that plays out or whether I'm just chatting shite again.

Depending on Nordi Mukiele's availability, that'll likely be our starting XI for Ipswich in a couple of weeks and I'm absolutely fine if that's the case.

There's obviously been a little bit of noise around the club's perceived inactivity in the transfer window. I would say I'm probably calmer than most about this, the club have very much earned that trust, however I'd be lying if I claimed a few small niggles hadn't started to creep in. Seeing the line-up yesterday and watching them go about their business, however, was the perfect antidote.

Given how monumental last season was, it feels odd that I'd momentarily forgotten how fucking class the Lads are. If we can't find value until later in the window and have to crack on for a few weeks with the XI that finished seventh and stuffed the Mags twice, so be it.

All in all, a hugely successful day at the office — although I did come away with one minor concern.

Watching Big Dan Ballard throw every fibre of his being towards any potential sign of danger is a joy; however, it does bring to mind the likelihood of him and Omar Alderete picking up niggly injuries here and there throughout the season and perhaps increases the need for defensive reinforcements more than I'd appreciated.

I'd normally try to end on a positive but, seeing as I've somehow talked myself into a negative space, I might as well go all in: the pink strip is crap.

Love the link up, loved the roll-out and love the idea of a man eating a load of burgers and dying on the toilet, but the actual kit? Rubbish. Just really hope we get to wear our home kit for the Europa League final.

title: Writer proposes trade that unloads Bronny James for young center
description: This mock trade would unload Bronny James and another young player who is stuck on the Lakers' bench for a young, defensive-minded backup center.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers reportedly would like to add one more center to their roster in order to have enough depth to absorb a potential injury to new starter Walker Kessler. They currently have Kevon Looney and Sandro Mamukelashvili slated as their backup centers, but neither can likely be counted on to play a significant number of minutes at the position should Kessler be unavailable for more than a few games.

Moussa Diabate of the Charlotte Hornets is a big man that Lakers reporter Jovan Buha recently said could be on the team's radar. He is 6-foot-10 and just 24 years of age, and while he weighs only 210 pounds, he has a wingspan of nearly 7-foot-3 and a decent 36.5-inch vertical leap.

Sai Mohan proposed a three-team trade that would give the Lakers Diabate, as well as young wing Liam McNeeley and a 2033 second-round draft pick for Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

"After three quiet seasons, Diabate flashed starter potential last year, setting career highs with 7.9 points and 8.7 rebounds across 73 games (47 starts) for the Hornets," Mohan wrote. "The 24-year-old Frenchman possesses the rim-running skill set to feed off Luka Doncic's playmaking — both in the half and fullcourt. Furthermore, he has shown the ability to be a solid rim protector, and was instrumental to the Hornets enjoying a midseason resurgence on the defensive end last year.

"Diabate would make an ideal backup to Walker Kessler, with the potential to share the floor alongside the Lakers' new starting center thanks to Kessler's expanding three-point range. At age 24, he also fits into the Lakers' new strategy to go younger and more agile after being criticized for being old and unathletic the last few years."

One would have to wonder why a promising team like the Hornets that got hot late last season would part with someone such as Diabate. Mohan gave a simple reason.

"Why would the Hornets agree to move on a young big with upside? It's simple — Diabate is an unrestricted free agent next year, and the Hornets need to choose between the Frenchman and Ryan Kalkbrenner as their center of the future. Most pundits would agree that the latter flashed more potential as a rookie and is worth investing in."

Diabate is owed $2.46 million for this coming season, so he could be an inexpensive get for Los Angeles if the Hornets are willing to play ball.

No matter how much James realistically improves this coming season, it is hard to imagine him getting any real playing time on the Lakers, given their solid guard depth, as well as their need to find playing time for promising rookie Cameron Carr.

While there are reports that the organization thinks highly of James, his best value to the team at this point could be as a trade asset of some sort.

The same is likely true of Knecht, who showed flashes of real promise as a rookie during the 2024-25 season but hasn't played well since. Some feel the wing, who was the No. 17 pick in the 2024 draft, is now a bust, but there could be a chance that he's salvageable on another team where he would actually get playing time.

In two NBA seasons, Knecht has averaged 7.1 points in 15.5 minutes a game while shooting 46% from the field and 36.8% from 3-point range.

title: Former Oilers 1st Overall Pick Taylor Hall Hits Major Life Milestone
description: The Edmonton Oilers selected forward Taylor Hall with the first overall selection in the 2010 NHL Draft, which was the first of three straight seasons picking first overall and four of five, culminating in 2015 with Connor McDavid.While Hall was a good player during his time with the Oilers, he never achieved anywhere close to […] The post Former Oilers 1st Overall Pick Taylor Hall Hits Major Life Milestone appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Edmonton Oilers selected forward Taylor Hall with the first overall selection in the 2010 NHL Draft, which was the first of three straight seasons picking first overall and four of five, culminating in 2015 with Connor McDavid.

While Hall was a good player during his time with the Oilers, he never achieved anywhere close to the kind of level that McDavid reached and currently plays at. Despite this, Hall has continued to be a solid contributor during most of his stops during his NHL career, which have now included several destinations.

As Oilers fans all know, Hall lifted the Stanley Cup earlier this spring with the Carolina Hurricanes, earning his first career championship ring. And with his personal day with the famed trophy, he informed his fans on social media that he's also achieved a life goal he spoke about earlier in his career.

For his own personal day with the Stanley Cup, Hall traveled to Ontario and held a special event at the Muskoka Lumber Community Centre, posing for pictures with throngs of fans.

He also took the Cup for a long-awaited boat ride; he posted a photo of himself piloting a small boat with the caption, "Boaters license secured✔️"

In 2011, while with the Oilers, Hall had written on social media that obtaining a boating license was something he's been wanting to do:

"Failed my boaters license again. I'm a joke I just want my license," he wrote in June 2011.

Not only has Hall achieved that life goal, but he's also got himself his first career Stanley Cup ring to boot. Not a bad summer for the former first overall pick.

Hall, who has played for multiple teams since his time with the Oilers, was acquired by the Hurricanes at the 2025 NHL Trade Deadline as part of a three-team deal involving Mikko Rantanen.

Carolina then re-signed him to a three-year, $9.5 million contract through 2028. In his first full season with the Hurricanes, Hall scored 23 goals with 31 assists, and added seven goals and 12 assists in 19 postseason games.

After taking his lap with the Cup at T-Mobile Arena, Hall was nearly speechless.

"I'm speechless. I'm tired and I'm speechless," Hall said. "It has been a journey, but that's life and that's the beautiful part of it — you just never know what turn is going to be the one that provides a memorable experience like this.

"I'm so happy. I'm so grateful that I was able to come here and fit in. I'm just thrilled."

Hall's goal in Game 6 against the Golden Knights proved to be the game-winner as part of their 3-0 shutout win.

"Winning with these guys is amazing; it's just a really special group," Hall said. "It's a group that allows players like myself to come in and have success. What they've done for the last seven or eight years here is amazing.

"I'm proud of the way I contributed, but it's easy here. We know how we need to play, and (Sunday) was a prime example of that. We were dialed in and I'm just a part of the process, but I was definitely happy that I was able to raise my game in the playoffs."

The playmakers are popping up rapidly for the Minnesota Vikings at the wide receiver position. Saturday was another big day for the group, as wide receiver Jeshaun Jones had a major day. Jones had multiple touchdowns on the day and was a very active target for both quarterbacks.

The Vikings need depth at the wide receiver position, and the wide receiver depth battle is coming down to either Jones or Dontae Fleming. On this day, Jones was able to catch touchdown passes from both J. J McCarthy and Kyler Murray, as the quarterback battle continues to take place. The throw from Murray to Jones in particular caught the eyes of many.

Kyler Murray threads the needle for the TD to Jeshaun Jones.

— VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 9, 2026

Jones' playmaking ability was evident at Maryland. Over the course of 48 games, he recorded 151 receptions for 2,040 yards and 14 touchdowns.

Breaking it down by year, Jones recorded 22 receptions for 271 yards and five touchdowns. He also had two rushing touchdowns and a passing touchdown. His best season came in 2023 when he recorded career-highs across the board. He had 56 catches for 790 yards and four touchdowns. This was when he was really able to show what he could do.

Underdog wide receivers excelling is becoming a theme at Vikings training camp. That is certainly not a bad thing. Taj Felton, also a former Maryland receiver, is playing at a high level as well. The Vikings are definitely top-heavy at the wide receiver spot. Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings all figured to be key figures for the wide receiver room. However, depth is extremely important, and this is where Jones could come in and make an impact.

Itâs not as though he is entirely new to the NFL either. He has paid his dues. He spent the first two seasons of his NFL career on the practice squad. title: Teen dog handler wins gold in final junior contest
description: The 17-year-old dog agility competitor says she now hopes to get selected for the adult team.
fullText:
A teenage dog handler who has helped bring home a gold medal from a world championships said she has left the British junior team on a high.

Taylor, 17, from Roade, Northamptonshire, along with her friend Isabella, 13, from Daventry, won the small team overall category in the Junior Open Agility World Championships, held in Germany.

Taylor ran a clear final round with her dog, Asher, to help clinch the title.

She said she was "really lucky" to do so well in her final year and now hoped to move into the senior squad.

She said the event in Mannheim "was a really good experience".

"When I was running it was a bit terrifying trying to make sure I went right, but it was really fun," said Taylor.

Due to her success in last month's event and her age, she will now compete in the second round of the adults' try-out stages.

"It gives us a good progression plan," she said.

Taylor has taken part in six junior Team GB events.

She made her debut in 2019, aged 10 and was the youngest competitor at the time.

In 2022, she competed in Finland and won both team and individual gold medals and became the U15 junior medium world champion.

The following year she won team gold; in 2024 she brought home a bronze medal, and last year her team won a jumping bronze.

Her family has six other dogs, despite her father being allergic to them.

Taylor was one of the four-strong GB team, including her fellow Northamptonshire competitor Isabella, to win the gold medal in the small team overall category.

Isabella competed with Hatti, her seven-year-old Staffordshire bull terrier, who she affectionately described as a little bit "psycho".

"She likes to bark at me when I'm running around - she sometimes likes to complain about sitting still," said Isabella.

She has three other dogs and said it was a "lot of work to train them".

"I'll be doing the junior try-outs again and hoping for another year on a team.

title: Andoni Iraola chat convinced La Liga star to make Liverpool move
description: Ronald Araujo to Liverpool: How Flick’s Call Opened Door to Anfield MoveLiverpool’s move for Ronald Araujo appears to have come together at remarkable speed, with SPORT.ES reporting that one conve...
fullText:
Liverpool's move for Ronald Araujo appears to have come together at remarkable speed, with SPORT.ES reporting that one conversation with Hansi Flick proved the decisive trigger in the Barcelona defender's fast-moving exit.

What had initially looked like a normal pre-season for Araujo, built on hard work, focus and a determination to reclaim a central role, shifted dramatically in a matter of days. The Uruguay international had approached the summer with full commitment, but clarity from Barcelona's head coach seems to have changed the direction of travel almost immediately.

For Liverpool, the timing is significant. Andoni Iraola has inherited a squad needing renewal in key positions, and central defence has clearly emerged as one of them. With Ibrahima Konate gone, and both Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez moving deeper into the later stages of their careers, the need for a high-level centre-back has been obvious. Araujo, if completed, would represent a major statement.

According to the report, Araujo sought honesty from Flick regarding his place in the pecking order. The response was direct. Despite being pleased with the defender's work and level during pre-season, Flick reportedly made it clear that Araujo was not projected to start the campaign as first-choice in central defence.

That message appears to have landed heavily. Barcelona's thinking, as outlined in the report, was shaped by a preference for a naturally left-sided central defender, while Pau Cubarsi is described as untouchable in the current structure. For a player of Araujo's stature, and one who has carried leadership responsibility as one of the club captains, the absence of firm guarantees over minutes was enough to prompt action.

There is no suggestion of a breakdown or any dramatic fallout. This reads more like a player receiving an honest sporting assessment, then deciding swiftly that his prospects lay elsewhere. In elite football, those moments matter. Once a senior player understands he may no longer be central to a manager's plan, the market tends to move quickly.

SPORT.ES states that Liverpool made contact with Araujo's representatives on Wednesday to explore the conditions of a deal. From there, events accelerated. Iraola is said to have spoken directly with the player, outlining the project and the role available to him at Anfield, specifically as part of a top-class defensive partnership alongside Van Dijk.

That level of direct manager involvement is often crucial in transfers of this scale. It can remove ambiguity, establish intent and reassure the player that he is not merely an option, but a target. In Araujo's case, the contrast between uncertainty in Barcelona and opportunity at Liverpool seems to have become increasingly clear.

Friday then emerged as the pivotal day. A remote meeting involving Liverpool, Barcelona, the player's camp and Araujo himself reportedly moved the process forward sharply. By late that evening, the report says the final approval had arrived, allowing the move to proceed.

The article also notes that Araujo kept matters private within the dressing room until Saturday morning, when he personally said goodbye to team-mates and coaching staff before Barcelona's trip to Italy. The plan, according to the report, is for him to travel to Liverpool on Sunday and begin work under Iraola on Monday.

If the move is finalised as expected, Liverpool would be adding a defender with high-level pedigree, physical authority and experience at the sharp end of major competition. Araujo has long been viewed as one of Europe's more imposing centre-backs, capable of defending aggressively, handling elite forwards and coping with pressure in big environments.

There will, of course, be interest in the exact structure of the agreement, especially with the source article referring to the move as a loan in one of its related story lines. That detail will matter once formal confirmation arrives. Either way, Liverpool appear to have acted decisively once the opening presented itself.

From Barcelona's side, this looks like a football decision shaped by squad planning and managerial preference. From Liverpool's side, it looks like opportunism backed by conviction. The club identified a need, found a player whose situation had changed, and moved before the market could become crowded.

For now, the expectation is clear. Ronald Araujo is closing in on Liverpool, and the catalyst, if this account is accurate, was not prolonged unrest or financial pressure, but a frank conversation that told him exactly where he stood.

As Liverpool fans, this is exactly the kind of move that gets pulses racing. Ronald Araujo is a serious defender, the sort who brings authority the moment he walks through the door. If Iraola has really moved this quickly and personally sold the project, that says plenty about how clear Liverpool's planning is right now.

There is every reason to be excited by the fit. Araujo has the athleticism, aggression and presence to thrive in the Premier League, and learning alongside Van Dijk could be massive for both the player and the team. Liverpool have needed a defensive refresh, and bringing in someone of this level feels like a proper answer rather than a stop-gap.

From a supporter's point of view, the most encouraging part is the decisiveness. Once it became clear the player was available, Liverpool went hard and fast. That is what top clubs do. They do not hang around waiting for the market to set the agenda for them.

If this gets completed smoothly, fans will rightly see it as a big signal from Iraola's new era. Araujo is experienced, hungry and clearly motivated by the chance to be central to a major project. That combination should excite Anfield. On paper, it looks like a defender who could become a huge favourite very quickly.

fullText:
Long-time UFC featherweight Darren Elkins officially retired from mixed martial arts following his fight at UFC Vegas 120.

The retirement was not a surprise, as Elkins previously announced he would be hanging up his gloves following his main card bout at UFC Vegas 120 against Yadier del Valle.

Unfortunately for Elkins, it was not a storybook ending as the veteran was brutally knocked out in just 35 seconds. But regardless, it's the end of one amazing career in the UFC for Elkins that began way back in 2010.

Thank you for the blood, sweat, and tears @DarrenElkinsMMA! pic.twitter.com/5gdxL0nF0b

The 42-year-old Elkins first began fighting in MMA back in 2007, going 10-1 on the Midwest regional circuit — including beating future Bellator MMA featherweight champion Pat Curran — before getting signed to the UFC in 2010.

He made his debut on the UFC Live: Vera vs. Jones card as a lightweight and defeated Duane Ludwig by TKO due to injury. In his second fight, Elkins fought and lost to future UFC legend Charles Oliveira due to submission. He then dropped down to featherweight and reeled off five straight wins before getting a big fight against top featherweight contender Chad Mendes, but a TKO loss to Mendes halted his ascent up the UFC featherweight ladder.

In 2017, Elkins had the biggest win of his UFC career to date when he came back in the third round and brutally knocked out top prospect Mirsad Bektic via third-round head kick KO in one of the biggest upsets and comebacks in UFC history.

Overall, Elkins finished his career with a 29-13 record, including an impressive 19-12 mark inside the Octagon, with many of those wins coming when he was the underdog.

The UFC also posted a career retrospective for Elkins, which you can watch below.

Congrats on a hell of a career @DarrenElkinsMMA. pic.twitter.com/el3Tff8hgv

During Elkins' UFC career, he won Fight of the Night once, he won Performance of the Night three times, and he had the second-most fights in UFC featherweight division history with 29. He also has the second-most wins in UFC featherweight division history behind Max Holloway.

Overall, Elkins had an underrated, phenomenal UFC career. Thank you for all the memories in the Octagon, Darren Elkins!

title: ‘Time is the key, they are young lads’ Matthias Jaissle reflects on first win ahead of huge season ahead
description: Matthias Jaissle saw his Newcastle United team win at their first attempt, against Valencia. Only a friendly of course but so important for NUFC to start building some momentum and confidence with the Premier League season only two weeks away now.
fullText:
Matthias Jaissle saw his Newcastle United team win at their first attempt, against Valencia.

Only a friendly of course but so important for NUFC to start building some momentum and confidence with the Premier League season only two weeks away now.

With Matthias Jaissle thrown in the deep end and such a turnover in the Newcastle United squad, so important for the new boss to see encouraging signs he can build on.

Going behind after only four minutes away from home against a team who finished top half of La Liga, no doubt plenty of Newcastle United fans feared the worst.

However, the Matthias Jaissle era saw the team show plenty of character to bounce back and win 2-1 with two second half goals from Yoane Wissa. Indeed, United could have been ahead by the break as Elanga had a goal disallowed that replays suggest wasn't offside and then Osula denied what looked a clear penalty.

Reflecting on the match and result Matthias Jaissle wanting to keep everybody grounded:*"We will not smash the locker room down and celebrate a lot, we are quite balanced. We know what this is about, it is pre-season and we still have a lot to do. We don't want to hang victories higher than they are and we also don't want to place losses lower than they should be. Next week there are things that we need to work on definitely but we did well in the camp [at La Manga] and in this friendly win."*

A ridiculous challenge/assault by Gaya on 35 minutes saw Anthony Elanga stretchered off and the Valencia captain sent off.

Everybody fearing a needless serious injury in a friendly but reassuring words from Matthias Jaissle: *"It was a shocking challenge and I was in fear [it was a serious injury], definitely. But now I'm more relaxed because the medical department are almost showing green lights that it is nothing serious. We are blessed. Hopefully he can be back in the next week. Anthony seems to be okay, that's the most important thing, that there is no serious injury as it looks right now."*

Matthias Jaissle talking more about the team performance: "Winning games always helps to gain confidence and we also knew that we had a hard week behind us. The players did well and there was a huge commitment in each session, so they really deserve two days off and then we start again. Time is the key, they are young lads. It's never going to be easy in football, especially at the highest level, but we're here to do that."

Nick Pope was part of the week's training camp but missing from the matchday squad against Valencia. Now that Lukas Hornicek has arrived and Ewen Jaouen as cover, it is expected now that Nick Pope will be allowed to move on.

Matthias Jaissle commenting on the NUFC keeper: *"I had a talk with Nick. I really appreciate what he did in his career so far, [but] he knows exactly the situation right now and we need to deal with it in the best possible way. But I always appreciate the player and the human being behind."*

Barcelona are currently involved in two of the most talked about transfer sagas in European football right now in Rodri and Julian Alvarez.

Rodri, in particular, has generated a lot of buzz in recent days after the midfielder chose to join Barcelona ahead of a move to Real Madrid.

Barcelona, though, must reach an agreement with Manchester City if they are to get their hands on the Spanish World Cup winner.

Rodri is keen on joining Barcelona. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

According to Diario SPORT, there is total optimism within Barcelona regarding their chances of signing Rodri, with the club now treating the midfielder as their absolute priority.

The Catalans have already presented an improved offer to Manchester City, having realised their initial proposal of €45 million plus €5 million in variables fell well short of the English club's demands.

The report cites sources within the club insist they are on the right track, with one claiming the most difficult steps have already been taken and that it is now simply a case of finishing the job.

The most significant of those steps, in Barcelona's eyes, has been securing the player's desire to join.

Rodri is understood to have already informed City directly that he wants to move to Barcelona, a crucial development that the club insist eliminates the risk of any late change of heart or rival hijack.

Barcelona are not underestimating Man City's negotiating position. (Photo by Annabel Lee-Ellis/Getty Images)

Despite the confidence, Barcelona are under no illusions about the challenge that lies ahead.

Rodri still belongs to City, and the Premier League champions hold the final say on any fee.

Barcelona are aware they cannot underestimate City's negotiating position, particularly given the initial bid never stood a realistic chance of getting the deal done.

The next offer is expected to move considerably closer to City's valuation, and Barcelona accept they will have to make a significant financial effort to turn their current optimism into a concrete agreement.

Still, the belief internally is that Rodri's determination to join will ultimately help bridge the gap.

For now, then, Barcelona wait, hopeful that one of the summer's most ambitious operations can be completed.

title: Death at a Funeral
description: Mariners lose 3-2 to Rays to mark 50 seasons of themselves
fullText:
I'm never sure what to think about 1995. I'm about the same age as Cal Raleigh, and neither of us had been born. I've picked up the key points over the years. Ken Griffey Jr. was cool. Edgar Martinez was wise. Randy Johnson was wild. Jay Buhner was bald. And Lou Piniella was pissed. These are the characters who saved baseball in Seattle. I can imagine the impact of that team through the voice of Dave Nieahus, through his reverence, his honesty. I can quantify their greatness in a spreadsheet. I can only smile politely when those clips are played.

But for all I've been told, for all my gentle nods, I've never been able to place Dan Wilson. He's always been there, as a player, an ambassador, a broadcaster or a coach; in all the pictures and at all the parties; forever standing in the background, affably. I'm not sure what he represents or how loud to clap. There are no clues in his FanGraphs' page or in his persona. There's nothing to discern in his Funko Pop—vacancy its lone identifying trait. I only know that he was there, and that he is here, sitting on my shelf, forever staring past me.

He's seen Olivo take his job, Sexson sulk, and Figgins in the outfield. He's seen the #6 Org, with its stomach bugs, soggy arms, sprinkler heads, and warning tracks; posers, brain spiders and broken promises. He's Believed in slogans and prospect lists and righteous indignation; Driveline and PEDs and left-on-left splits. He's seen greatness come and quickly go, or stay too long, or return and spoil. Too many characters to list, too few to remember, most summed up in a word. I'll let you pick.

These are my Mariners. The naughts. A symbol more than a celebration. Decorated with baseball, rather than embodying it. Forever looking towards a time that doesn't exist. I display them in my life not quite with pride but a perverse sense of duty, or marketing, or irony, or yes maybe pride. Never, ever the protagonists.

Still, I watch. I write. I give myself, for a glimpse behind those plastic eyes. To see what they see. To know this team. To stay just a few more years.

Suddenly it's there, in a blink, in a lifetime.

The Mariners honored 50 players before Saturday's game to celebrate their 50th season. It was a fairly predictable ceremony, as the team seems to find something to celebrate in this fashion once a summer. It was nice.

The University of Washington marching band kicked things off with the Mariners nautical theme song, before diving into their pep band set list for what felt like a bit too long. A hype reel followed, with the standard fare of classic highlights and a voice over delivering the first platitudes of the evening.

They eventually got to the point and announced the 50 most notable Mariners alumni. Players were brought out by era, old guys first. The full list wasn't too surprising or controversial. It was cool to see guys I wasn't thinking about ahead of time, like JJ Putz, Kazuhiro Sasaki, and Raul Ibanez. And it was cool to see some personal favorites, like Mitch Haniger, James Paxton, and Hisashi Iwakuma. The cheers outweighed the boos for Alex Rodriguez and Dan Wilson. The only living players who didn't show up were Robinson Canó, Kyle Seager, Freddy García, and Luis Castillo. There were seven players from the active roster (and eight if you count Castillo). The only snub I could think of was Eugenio Suárez, but I understand why he wasn't included. After they called 40 or so names chronologically, they brought out the inner circle guys like Alvin Davis, Jay Buhner, and Félix Hernández. They finished by having the quartet of true Hall of Famers (Ken Griffey Jr., Edgar Martinez, Randy Johnson, and Ichiro) walk in from center field. Again, it was nice.

Next came a longer montage on the history of the team. This one was great, I thought, with much more than the standard highlights you've seen too often. They showcased lots of great Mariners-y things, like individual performances and minor accolades and commercials. Rick Rizzs did the voice over with another round of platitudes.

The video faded to the podium with a tuxedo'd Rizzs offering a few more platitudes before handing the mic to Alvin Davis. I was excited for this, as we generally don't get to hear from Davis, despite his status as Mr. Mariner. His speech was OK. He talked about the Mariners identity: "Loyal, steady, kind — that's a Mariner." And he noted the org's tendency to hold on for dear life to its history, pointing to Wilson and Edgar in the dugout. He eventually fell into the corny routine of trying to hype up the current squad and told them to go win a World Series. "Outsiders have doubted this franchise for 40 years (sic). Let that doubt fuel you. Prove them wrong. We believe in you. Prove us right."

John Stanton was next to the stage, the boos covered with yet another highlight package, this time honoring Rizzs. But instead of more platitudes, Stanton got right to the point. He thanked Rizzs for 41 years with the team and announced he would be inducted into the Mariners Hall of Fame. "For many Mariners fans, the voice of the summer is Rick Rizzs," Stanton said. This was a very touching moment, with the players and crowd giving a tremendous ovation while Rizzs failed to fight back tears.

Rizzs took the podium again, clearly flustered by the news — again, very touching. He thanked a bunch of people and quipped he was honored to be the "shortest member of the Mariners Hall of Fame." Rizzs then announced Lou Piniella, who was yet to be seen, would throw out the first pitch to Wilson. Piniella appeared and all the players got off the stage and huddled around him while he made the toss. This was the best part of the night, as all the alums stood in the middle of the field and commiserated. A-Rod gave Wilson a huge hug. Haniger and J.P. did some catching up. Mike Moore talked Logan Gilbert's ear off. Buhner and Félix exchanged a chummy embrace. Dave Valle was mic'd up. For as much as these things can be a bit of an eye roll, given the frequency with which the organization insists on remembering itself, seeing all these people again was a good time. It was nice.

Then the game began. Turns out it was still the 2026 Mariners. They lost 3-2.

George Kirby got the start, shortly after being named one of the 50. He was just OK. He couldn't find the zone at times and struggled to coax much chase or whiff at others, with the Rays fouling off tons of pitches. He nearly made it through four innings with a 1-0 lead, but with two outs, Victor Mesa Jr. got hold of an up-and-in fastball and crushed a game-tying homer to right. A pair of singles followed and things looked like they might get away for Kirby. But he got a pop up in foul territory that Cal Raleigh made a fantastic sliding catch on, despite a competing effort from Kirby.

Michael Rucker took the ball for the sixth. It wasn't pretty. He loaded the bases on an error from Brendan Donovan, a single, and a walk. Richie Palacios battled and battled and picked up a two-out, two-strike single to plate a pair of runs and give the Rays a 3-1 lead. They wouldn't score again, and they wouldn't need to.

The Mariners offense wasn't terrible, but it certainly wasn't enough. Casey Legumina got the start for the Rays, the first leg in a bullpen day (starter Griffin Jax was scratched with an injury shortly before the game). Legumina got the ball to Cam Booser with one out in the second inning, the game still tied at zero. Naylor quickly changed that, taking Booser deep on the first pitch he threw.

Donovan immediately singled and Raleigh walked, and it looked like the Mariners might have a chance for a big inning with just one out. But they were turned away from there. Then they went in order in the third. Naylor picked up a double in the fourth, but nothing came of it. Then they went in order in the fifth and sixth. They wouldn't get another base runner until Naylor went deep again in the seventh. It was a three extra base hit day for Naylor, the lone bright spot in this one.

Things got heated in the sixth. Julio Rodríguez struck out looking on a pitch out of the zone to end the inning. Julio immediately — and I mean immediately — tapped his head to challenge. The ump said he didn't challenge in time, which wasn't true. It seemed the ump wasn't paying attention. Julio started to give him the business, before Dan Wilson came crashing in, kicking and screaming, about as livid as I've ever seen him. Wilson eventually got run, and Manny Acta jumped in to drag him away. But Acta midway through heard something from the umpire he didn't like either and started yelling himself. Eventually the crew chief came over and escorted them back to the dugout.

The episode turned the game over to the boo birds, who'd been booing the team generally the last few home games and were now booing every pitch called by the umpire. It didn't help the Rays asked for (and were granted) a challenge in the next inning. This gave the evening a sour taste, which was fitting on a night meant to celebrate what's been one of the most disappointing seasons for a franchise with so many of them.

Still, keeping with the theme, the Mariners offered just enough hope to keep you watching. Down 3-2, Cole Young led off the eighth with a single. But Randy Arozarena nearly hit into a double play, and Dominic Canzone did hit into a double play to end the threat. Julio led off the ninth with a single. But Naylor just missed another homer and Donovan hit into a double play to wrap things up. It was another near miss. The Mariners fell to 56-62 and four games out of the AL West.

And so that was it. A nice ceremony for some nice people, followed by a Mariners loss. See you at 100.

title: The F1 careers shaped by new Red Bull junior boss Gwen Lagrue
description: Red Bull Junior Programme’s future director Gwen Lagrue, much like Helmut Marko, has built a reputation over the years for identifying and developing a number of promising talents who later established themselves in Formula 1. fullText:
Red Bull Junior Programme's future director Gwen Lagrue, much like Helmut Marko, has built a reputation over the years for identifying and developing a number of promising talents who later established themselves in Formula 1. But who are they, and how many drivers has he helped on their way to the top?

While Helmut Marko helped shape a generation of drivers who went on to become some of Formula 1's biggest stars, most notably Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen, Lagrue can also boast an impressive track record of his own. He will effectively take over the Austrian's role in identifying and developing the next generation of outstanding talents for the Milton Keynes-based team's junior programme.

While Kimi Antonelli and George Russell are now well known as the two leading products of Mercedes' junior system since the creation of its young driver programme, Lagrue also played a key role in identifying and developing other talents who remain on the Formula 1 grid today.

Lagrue first became involved in Ocon's career long before either of them became part of the Mercedes set-up. With the Frenchman's family struggling to cover the considerable costs of climbing the junior single-seater ladder, Eric Boullier saw enough potential in Ocon to connect him with Lagrue, who was working for Gravity Sport Management at the time. The Lotus/Renault-linked organisation subsequently stepped in to provide the financial and management support Ocon needed to continue his progression through the lower categories.

Their paths remained closely linked when Ocon became associated with Mercedes in 2015. Around the same period, Lagrue also joined the German manufacturer and later took responsibility for its young-driver programme. His involvement with Ocon continued throughout the following years, including after the Frenchman established himself elsewhere.

Ocon ultimately never became a Mercedes F1 race driver, but his career still represents one of the earliest examples of a talent whose rise was closely supported by Lagrue. Nearly a decade after making his Formula 1 debut, the Frenchman has become a constant presence on the grid.

The Thai is another current Formula 1 driver whose path crossed closely with Lagrue well before reaching the top category. The pair first became acquainted during Albon's karting career, where he emerged as one of the standout names of a highly rated generation that also featured Max Verstappen. When the programme supporting Albon chose to part ways with him at the end of 2012, Lagrue stepped in and offered him an opportunity within the Lotus set-up.

Their relationship continued as Albon progressed through Formula Renault, Formula 3, GP3 and Formula 2, with Lagrue supporting him throughout those stages. Albon also completed simulator work for Mercedes before being released when the opportunity arose for him to return to the young driver programme that previously dropped him.

In a lengthy post on social media, Lagrue looked back on his 11-year journey with Mercedes following his final Grand Prix with the team in Hungary, placing particular emphasis on the drivers he helped nurture during his time in charge of the junior programme. Among them were Esteban Ocon, Nyck de Vries, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, alongside Fred Vesti, Doriane Pin and the many other young talents who passed through the Mercedes system over the years.

For Lagrue, seeing those drivers develop and progress towards the highest levels of motorsport was one of the most rewarding aspects of his role. He encouraged the current and former members of the programme to continue pursuing their ambitions, working hard and making the most of every stage of their journey, while underlining the importance of the team surrounding them in helping them reach their full potential.

Rather than focusing on Mercedes' championships, victories and records, Lagrue highlighted the people he worked with and the opportunity to guide young drivers through crucial stages of their careers as the most meaningful part of his time with the team. He also expressed his gratitude to Toto Wolff for the trust placed in him and thanked the entire Mercedes organisation, bringing an 11-season chapter to a close before moving on to the next stage of his career.

title: Lakers urged not to sign $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, focus on Klay Thompson, PJ Washington
description: The Los Angeles Lakers have been all in on a young NBA champion. However, it now seems like they are being told to move onto potential trades for either Klay Thompson or PJ Washington.
fullText:
Lakers urged not to sign $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, focus on Klay Thompson, PJ Washington originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Los Angeles Lakers have been all-in on Jonathan Kuminga since LeBron James informed the team that he would no longer be returning. However, it has been a lengthy process for Los Angeles to get a deal done.

Even throughout this process, the Lakers have not wavered and remain focused on Kuminga. Landing a deal for the young forward remains LA's top priority as the offseason continues.

"Jonathan Kuminga remains the Lakers' top free agent target before finishing their offseason. As the Cavaliers have pivoted to chasing Peyton Watson, Kuminga is the sole focus currently for Los Angeles. There could soon be momentum gathering on Kuminga to LA via sign-and-trade," NBA reporter Evan Sidery wrote.

With the Lakers seemingly being Kuminga's preferred destination, it still appears that his camp and the Atlanta Hawks are creating obstacles to a potential sign-and-trade. Nothing has moved in weeks, largely because Atlanta has not been satisfied with the trade package it could receive in return.

"It has reached the second month of what has become a second consecutive prolonged Kuminga free agency process. The Lakers met with Kuminga in the early hours of free agency, pitching him on a high-minutes role for a high-profile fringe contender in desperate need of athletic help on the wing. The opportunity appealed to Kuminga, but the sign-and-trade contract offer (years, money, package going back to Atlanta) didn't satisfy all sides. The Lakers remain interested in him, league sources said, but movement toward a deal has remained stalled for weeks," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote.

With the process continuing to drag on, the Lakers have now been urged to move on from Kuminga and prioritize a trade for either Klay Thompson or P.J. Washington.

"Obviously, anything can change during the NBA offseason, as Kuminga could have a change of heart or decide Los Angeles is the best situation for him, but it seems like it is time for the storied franchise to move on. Perhaps the Lakers should focus on trading for Klay Thompson or P.J. Washington, both of whom have experience playing with Doncic," SI's Ryan Ward wrote.

At this point, it is fair to say that moving on from Kuminga would not necessarily be a bad idea. The Lakers have been pursuing him for nearly two months, and nothing has been finalized.

Kuminga was on a $46 million contract last season, while the Lakers are looking for someone who can make an immediate impact. It remains unclear whether Kuminga would be able to do that right away, but Thompson and Washington have already proven themselves throughout their careers.

For the Lakers, the decision ultimately comes down to how long they are willing to wait for Kuminga versus how quickly they can find another option to strengthen the roster around Luka Doncic.

title: Elina Svitolina Makes Feelings Known on Beating Amanda Anisimova in Toronto – ‘I Was Expecting Her To Come Back’
description: Elina Svitolina has advanced to the quarterfinals of the 2026 Canadian Open, triumphing over Amanda Anisimova in a blockbuster fourth-round clash. After securing a comfortable victory, Svitolina shared her thoughts on her battle with the American.
fullText:
Elina Svitolina has advanced to the quarterfinals of the 2026 Canadian Open, triumphing over Amanda Anisimova in a blockbuster fourth-round clash. After securing a comfortable victory, Svitolina shared her thoughts on her battle with the American.

After triumphing over Jéssica Bouzas Maneiro and Anastasia Potapova, No. 9 seed Svitolina set up a highly anticipated battle with No. 8 seed Anisimova in the fourth round of the WTA 1000 event in Toronto.

Entering the contest with a 4-1 lead in her head-to-head record against Anisimova, Svitolina continued her dominance over the American at the Canadian Open. She raced through the opening set and went up a double break in the second. Although Anisimova fought back to save four match points, Svitolina held her nerve to secure a 6-2, 6-4 victory.

During her post-match press conference, Svitolina acknowledged that she struggled to close out the second set. She praised Anisimova as a formidable player and said that she had expected the American to make a stronger comeback before expressing satisfaction at emerging victorious.

"Yeah, it was not easy to close that second set. I think she came back, she was playing a bit better. It was not easy, with a little bit of wind, and the nature of the game, was not an easy one," Svitolina said.

"So, yeah, I mean, she is, of course, a hell of a player, so I was expecting her to come back a little bit more. Sometimes she's playing really sharp. So, yeah, it was not an easy one, but I'm really happy with the way I could handle the 5-4 and serve it out to close the match," she added.

Svitolina also reflected on her own campaign at the WTA 1000 event, pointing out the improvements she had made since edging out a hard-fought 6-7(5), 7-6(4), 6-4 victory over Jéssica Bouzas Maneiro in her opening match.

"Well, I think I improved match by match. The second round was not the best performance from my side. But I'm happy that I went through that tough battle. Having one day off I think helped me to again find my game, work on few things, and feeling better on the court. Also physically, one day off is helping me to just be more fresh," she said.

Up next, Elina Svitolina will take on No. 16 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova in the quarterfinals of the Canadian Open. Meanwhile, Amanda Anisimova will begin gearing up for the Cincinnati Open, aiming to make a deeper run at the WTA 1000 event, which begins on August 13.
